L001.title: Board & coordinates
L001.question: What is the file in e4?
L001.body: On the board, columns are named a-h and rows are numbered 1-8.

L002.title: Light and dark squares
L002.question: What color is h1?
L002.body: The bottom-right corner of the board is a light square.

L003.title: Pawn first move
L003.question: How many squares may a pawn advance on its first move?
L003.body: A pawn may advance one or two squares from its starting square.

L004.title: Pawn captures
L004.question: How does a pawn capture?
L004.body: A pawn captures an enemy piece on the square diagonally ahead.

L005.title: Knight movement
L005.question: Which piece can jump over pieces?
L005.body: A knight moves two squares in one direction and one square at a right angle, and can jump over pieces.

L006.title: Bishop movement
L006.question: How does a bishop move?
L006.body: A bishop moves diagonally and stays on the color of its starting square.

L007.title: Rook movement
L007.question: Which directions can a rook move?
L007.body: A rook moves horizontally and vertically.

L008.title: Queen movement
L008.question: How does a queen move?
L008.body: The queen moves like a rook and a bishop combined.

L009.title: King movement
L009.question: How far does a king move normally?
L009.body: The king moves to any adjacent square that is not under attack.

L010.title: Check
L010.question: What must you do in check?
L010.body: If your king is attacked, you must remove the threat.

L011.title: Checkmate
L011.question: What ends a game with a winner?
L011.body: If the king is attacked and has no legal escape, it is checkmate.

L012.title: Stalemate
L012.question: What is stalemate?
L012.body: If the player to move has no legal move and is not in check, it is stalemate.

L013.title: Castling rules
L013.question: Which pieces move in castling?
L013.body: In castling the king and rook move together; the king may not pass through an attacked square.

L014.title: En passant
L014.question: When is en passant available?
L014.body: En passant is a special right to capture a pawn that has just advanced two squares, available only on the very next move.

L015.title: Promotion
L015.question: Which is a legal promotion?
L015.body: A pawn reaching the last rank can be promoted to a queen, rook, bishop or knight.

L016.title: Piece values
L016.question: Which piece is usually worth five?
L016.body: Approximate values: pawn 1, knight/bishop 3, rook 5, queen 9.

L017.title: Center control
L017.question: Which square is central?
L017.body: The squares e4, d4, e5 and d5 are important in the opening.

L018.title: Development
L018.question: Which is good opening practice?
L018.body: Bring your knights and bishops to active squares.

L019.title: King safety
L019.question: What helps king safety?
L019.body: To keep the king safe, usually castle in good time.

L020.title: Tempo
L020.question: What is tempo in chess?
L020.body: With a move that forces a reply, you can gain time.

L021.title: Fork
L021.question: What is a fork?
L021.body: One piece attacks two or more targets at once.

L022.title: Pin
L022.question: What is a pin?
L022.body: If a pinned piece moves, a more valuable piece behind it is endangered.

L023.title: Skewer
L023.question: What is a skewer?
L023.body: When the valuable piece moves away, the piece behind it may be lost.

L024.title: Double check
L024.question: How many pieces attack in double check?
L024.body: Two pieces give check at the same time.

L025.title: Discovered attack
L025.question: What creates a discovered attack?
L025.body: When the front piece moves, the attack of the piece behind it is revealed.

L026.title: Hanging piece
L026.question: What is a hanging piece?
L026.body: An unprotected piece creates a tactical opportunity.

L027.title: Back rank
L027.question: What is a back-rank weakness?
L027.body: If the king has no escape squares, a back-rank mating threat can arise.

L028.title: Mating net
L028.question: What is a mating net?
L028.body: Several pieces cover the king's escape squares.

L029.title: Queen and king mate
L029.question: What helps queen mate?
L029.body: The queen restricts the king's space; support her with your own king.

L030.title: Rook and king mate
L030.question: What helps rook mate?
L030.body: Use the rook to restrict the enemy king and bring your own king closer.

L031.title: Opposition
L031.question: Where is opposition important?
L031.body: When the kings face each other, whose turn it is can be critical.

L032.title: Passed pawn
L032.question: What is a passed pawn?
L032.body: A pawn with no opposing pawn in front that could stop it.

L034.title: Isolated pawn
L034.question: What is an isolated pawn?
L034.body: There are no friendly pawns on the adjacent files.

L035.title: Doubled pawns
L035.question: What are doubled pawns?
L035.body: Two pawns of the same color stand on the same file.

L036.title: Open file
L036.question: What is an open file?
L036.body: A file with no pawns on it.

L037.title: Semi-open file
L037.question: What is a semi-open file?
L037.body: A file with no pawn of one player.

L038.title: Active rook
L038.question: Where are rooks often active?
L038.body: Rooks can be effective on open files and on the seventh rank.

L039.title: Bishop pair
L039.question: Where is bishop pair often strong?
L039.body: Two bishops can be strong in open positions.

L040.title: Good and bad bishop
L040.question: What blocks a bad bishop?
L040.body: A bishop blocked by its own pawn chain may lose effectiveness.

L041.title: Knight outpost
L041.question: What makes an outpost?
L041.body: A knight on an advanced square that pawns cannot chase away is strong.

L042.title: Calculation
L042.question: What comes first in calculation?
L042.body: Examine candidate moves and forced replies in order.

L043.title: Exchanges
L043.question: What matters in exchanges?
L043.body: Before an exchange, evaluate the resulting position and piece values.

L044.title: Planning
L044.question: What guides a plan?
L044.body: Form a short plan based on the strengths and weaknesses of the position.

L045.title: Active king
L045.question: What should king do in endgame?
L045.body: In the endgame the king is an active fighting piece.

L046.title: Zugzwang
L046.question: What is zugzwang?
L046.body: Having to move can worsen a player's position.

L047.title: Draw conditions
L047.question: Which can be a draw?
L047.body: Stalemate, insufficient material, repetition and move-count rules can lead to a draw.

L048.title: Review habit
L048.question: What improves learning?
L048.body: After a game, examine your critical moves and missed chances.
